claim: On leaf-classification, isolating opus to the tuner role only (X002: tuner=opus, all other 7 roles=sonnet) FAILS to bridge bronze→silver. The mixed routing achieved above_median (one tier BELOW sonnet's bronze) at $26 — slightly worse than all-sonnet baseline ($21, bronze).
scope: Single experiment, single task. The negative finding is specific to leaf-classification (FGVC image task). Does NOT prove tuner-opus is useless in general — only that it does not localize the silver-vs-bronze quality gap on this task.
limitations: n=1 for the X002 routing. Score gap to baseline sonnet is tiny (0.01642 vs 0.01364 — same order of magnitude); could easily be variance, not a true regression. Need a re-run before claiming X002 is strictly worse than baseline.
We do not yet know which role IS the bridge. Next experiments should isolate coder, then designer.
Cost accounting reports manager=$0 again (E005 re-observed). Opus-tuner only added ~$7 over the baseline tuner cost (~$11), much less than the $30+ gap between all-sonnet and all-opus runs.
policy_recommendation: Do NOT add tuner-opus-only as a routing option for image-classification-small. The cost is similar to all-sonnet but medal tier is no better. Keep all-sonnet as the family default until coder-isolation experiment runs.
next_actions: X002b: coder=opus, everything-else=sonnet on leaf-classification. Tests whether coder is the silver-vs-bronze bridge.
If X002b also fails: try designer=opus, then 2-role mixes.

downgrades.E004: indirectly weakened — the 'opus bridges tier' claim might be a coder+tuner+designer joint effect, not localizable to any single role
